extracted.intended_audience: EMBO community: researchers, applicants for EMBO funding, EMBO Press authors, reviewers and selection committee members
extracted.subtask_short: EMBO policies for funding and publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Organization-wide policy summary describing the standards EMBO applies to its funding programmes and EMBO Press publications, covering open science, data and methods, research integrity, responsible assessment, equality/diversity, sustainability, conflicts of interest, and AI use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access encouragement and APC support
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO encourages funded researchers and members of the EMBO community to publish their results in journals that have rigorous and transparent peer review processes and to publish Open Access. The EMBO Press journals have been published exclusively Open Access since January 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are schemes offering financial support for publication fees at EMBO Press journals, such as tiered Article Processing Charge (APC) pricing, fee waivers for scientists within the EMBO increasing participation scheme, additional support for authors in India, and waivers and charge reductions on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licencing recommendations for publications
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO encourages use of an Open Access-compliant licence that facilitates sharing of scientific information and mandates citation of the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO recommends choosing licences with the following features: Attribution (users must attribute the contribution in the manner specified), Non-commercial (users may not use contribution for commercial purposes), and No derivative works (users may not alter, transform, or build upon this work). Frequently used Creative Commons licences (CC BY and CC BY non-derivative) protect the authors’ moral rights. Any licence condition can be waived if users obtain permission from the copyright holder; for reuse/distribution, link to the Creative Commons webpage is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data licensing recommendation (CC0 for data)
rubrics_metrics.description: For data, EMBO recommends using a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC0 removes legal barriers to re-use and mining of research data. According to standard scholarly practice, it is recommended to provide appropriate citation and attribution whenever technically possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and peer reviewed preprints encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO encourages researchers to make research results public as soon as possible by posting on recognised preprint servers and to use preprint peer review services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognised servers examples: arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Zenodo, OSF, PeerJ. EMBO also encourages use of preprint peer review services such as Review Commons and some scientific journals, and to make peer review reports generally available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting preprints in funding applications (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Fellows and Young Investigator programmes accept first or last author research papers with “in submission” status by the application deadline (must be accepted by interview date). EMBO also accepts first or last author preprints posted online alongside authenticated reviewer reports provided conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) Preprint posted on a recognized community preprint server (e.g., arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Zenodo, OSF, PeerJ); (2) peer reviews must be publicly available online; (3) peer reviews were verifiably obtained from an independent preprint peer review service such as Review Commons and some journals; (4) the reviews provide an in-depth and independent expert analysis of the rigor, validity, and contribution of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID requirement for discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO requires funding applicants to submit their ORCID iD to ensure unambiguous name assignment and improve discoverability of published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO Press signed a joint statement to encourage ORCID adoption. Authors are encouraged to register; corresponding authors are required to supply their ORCID iD upon submission of a revised manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition in FAIR-aligned repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO encourages researchers to deposit source data, metadata, methods, and protocols in recognized public repositories that align with the FAIR principles (findability, accessibility, interoperability, reusability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources to identify suitable repositories include ELIXIR and FAIRsharing (links provided). Repositories provide persistent identifiers and stable resolvable links to data to improve reproducibility, trust, and re-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMBO Press requirement: submit source data for all figures
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press requires authors to submit source data for all figures depicting experimental results and to use structured methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO Press encourages describing methods using a step-by-step protocol format and depositing protocols in protocols.io to increase reproducibility and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for responsible conduct of research
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Members, awardees, staff and EMBO-funded researchers are expected to observe the fundamental principles in the European Code of Conduct for Research Integrity: reliability, honesty, respect, and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability refers to quality of research design, methodology, analysis and resource use. Honesty covers transparent, fair, full and unbiased development, undertaking, reviewing, reporting and communicating of research. Respect covers colleagues, participants, society, ecosystems and cultural heritage. Accountability covers management, organization, training, supervision, and wider impacts. Awardees/authors must also adhere to national/institutional standards and international guidelines (e.g., WMA Declaration of Helsinki, Belmont Report, US HHS ORI) and may be asked to provide evidence of conformity to applicable regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory research integrity training for certain awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of receiving funding, EMBO Postdoctoral Fellows and Young Investigators are required to take an online research integrity course co-developed by EMBO; awardees in other schemes are encouraged to take such a course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO expects outputs from its membership and awardees to pass rigorous research integrity screening and adhere to reproducibility standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics checks and misconduct screening by EMBO Press
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure reliability of research, EMBO Press staff conduct routine analyses of images and data submitted with manuscripts and assess suspected instances of scientific fraud or other misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed issues include inappropriate image manipulation or processing, plagiarism, data misrepresentation, duplicate publication, and other potential misconduct. Full policy on research integrity and misconduct is available on EMBO Press website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible research assessment: avoid journal metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO adheres to principles of responsible research assessment and instructs reviewers to avoid relying on journal impact factors or other publication-based metrics when evaluating applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are instructed to avoid indicating JIF or any publication-based metrics in their publication list. The aim is to focus reviewers’ attention on paper content rather than journal metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants to summarise their best papers and justify selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are asked to summarise and highlight why they chose their best papers: two papers for Installation Grants; three papers for Young Investigators, Postdoctoral Fellowships, and Global Investigator Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to focus review on the content and contribution of selected works rather than venue-based metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of selection processes and committee membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for EMBO funding schemes are publicly available and provide detailed descriptions of criteria used within each programme; names of selection committee members are published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board membership is balanced to create gender, expertise, and geographical diversity. Public availability of procedures promotes transparency in assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct and unconscious bias mitigation for committees
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO has a code of conduct with expectations for selection committee members and primes committee members before meetings on unconscious bias and conflicts related to unconscious bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priming includes how to become aware of unconscious bias and how it may affect decision-making. This supports fair and informed decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest policy
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO and EMBO Press have policies regarding actual and perceived conflicts of interest, including personal, professional, and financial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full policies are provided on linked pages for EMBO selection committees and EMBO Press competing interests; committee members and reviewers must follow these policies to manage COIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality, diversity and inclusion commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO is committed to equity, gender balance and equal opportunity across selection committees, referee panels, applicants, awardees, staff and conference speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO committees and Council average ~30% members of underrepresented genders; EMBO implements measures (e.g., priming on unconscious bias) to facilitate fair decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental sustainability for conferences and meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO implements measures to reduce the environmental impact of in-person meetings and awards sustainability badges to meetings that implement sustainability measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO encourages organisers to consider hybrid options, and workshop/conference organisers can apply for additional EMBO funding to implement sustainability measures. See the sustainable conferencing section for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of AI tool use in application preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO acknowledges value of AI tools in preparing grant applications but requires applicants to be fully and solely responsible for originality and accuracy of their applications and requests disclosure of whether and which AI tools were used and for what purpose for Fellowship Programme applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should disclose e.g., use of AI to improve language style or other specific purposes; EMBO will update this policy as generative AI develops.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use and authorship rules for EMBO Press submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: An AI or LLM programme cannot be listed as an author. Use of AI programmes should be primarily restricted to improving style, accessibility or quality of human-generated text and images; any AI-assembled part must be thoroughly checked and verified by the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors bear full responsibility for all text and images including factual accuracy, completeness, and accurate literature citation. Authors must ensure AI does not lead to plagiarism, misrepresentation, falsification, or infringement of third-party rights, and must disclose AI use in the published article, including which parts were assisted and which tools were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-specific rules for data, figures, and synthetic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Data figures and schemata must be original or, if illustrative, accurately cite the source. AI programmes can be used in collection and analysis of data if documented in the Methods. Synthetic data generated by AI must be clearly labeled in the main text and figure and documented in the Methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI must not be used to synthesize or edit experimental data in a manner that misrepresents findings. AI may be used for illustrative purposes if declared and attribution is provided where appropriate.
